lede.headline: Zuckerberg wants to own the device you talk to AI through
lede.dek: Meta unveiled $1,299 VR glasses, new Ray-Bans and a keychain gadget called Muse Charm, all built around its Muse AI agent. Forbes says Meta's rising stock has pushed Zuckerberg into the world's top five.

top10AsOf: Net worths per Forbes as of Sept 1, 2026. Rankings move daily: Forbes reported Zuckerberg climbing into the top five on Sept 23.

stories.headline: Meta bets on AI you wear, carry and shop with
stories.move: At Meta Connect on Sept 23, Meta showed $1,299 VR Glasses, third-generation Ray-Ban Meta glasses, audio-only glasses and Muse Charm, a keychain-sized device for talking to its Muse AI agent.
stories.why: Meta is building hardware around its AI agent, which it says will work with retailers like Walmart and Instacart. Whoever owns the device you ask AI to buy things through owns a lot of future commerce.
stories.bear: The VR Glasses cost $1,299 and don't go on sale until spring 2027. Meta also agreed to an $18B settlement in August over claims its apps were designed to addict kids.
stories.watch: Meta's developer sessions today, then its third-quarter earnings in late October.

stories.headline: Trump hosts Xi today, and Nvidia's China business is on the table
stories.move: Trump hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House today, with AI on the agenda. Huang is expected at tonight's state dinner.
stories.why: Nvidia's $108B forecast for this quarter assumes zero data-center chip sales to China. Any opening would be pure upside to a number the market already has.
stories.bear: Beijing has pushed its tech companies toward homegrown chips, and Nvidia says it needs approval from both governments, not just Washington, to sell a competitive product there.
stories.watch: Any export or AI agreement announced tonight or tomorrow.

stories.headline: Ellison scraps his plan to sell up to $7.5B of Oracle
stories.move: A filing on Sept 11 showed Ellison could sell up to 50 million Oracle shares through Oct 24. On Sept 12 he cancelled the plan. No shares were sold, and Oracle says he has no other plans to sell.
stories.why: He controls more than 40% of Oracle and has almost never sold. Walking the plan back within a day tells the market he is staying all-in on Oracle's AI infrastructure bet.
stories.bear: He adopted the plan back on June 22, so selling was on the table for months. He has also stepped back from Oracle's earnings calls this year.
stories.watch: Any Form 4 filings, and how Oracle's new co-CEOs, Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia, handle the AI spending.

stories.headline: Buffett steps down as Berkshire chairman
stories.move: On Sept 18, Buffett stepped down as chairman and became chairman emeritus, staying on the board. His son Howard Buffett is the new chairman. Greg Abel has been CEO since January.
stories.why: Abel now fully owns Berkshire's next moves, and the company had $365.5B in cash at the end of June. He stepped up buybacks to $4.5B last quarter.
stories.bear: Berkshire stock is up only about 1% this year while the S&P 500 has gained more than 11%. Buffett also slipped out of Forbes' top 10 in August.
stories.watch: Berkshire's third-quarter report in early November: buybacks, new stakes and the cash balance.

stories.headline: SpaceX shares slide back toward their IPO price
stories.move: SpaceX closed at $148.36 on Sept 23, down from $154.72 the day before. It listed at $135 on June 12 in the largest IPO ever, raising about $75B.
stories.why: The stock sits roughly 10% above its offer price and about a third below its 52-week high of $225.64. Early buyers have mostly given back the debut pop.
stories.bear: Hot IPOs often lag the market in their first years, and SpaceX is spending heavily on Starship, satellites and AI compute.
stories.watch: SpaceX's next earnings report, scheduled for Nov 5.

consensus.headline: The top 10 are buying their way deeper into AI
consensus.body: Two tracked billionaires made big moves to own more of the AI stack this month.

watch: Today: Trump and Xi meet at the White House. Watch for any change to Nvidia's China chip sales.
quickHits: Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $12.9B, its second-biggest deal ever.
Buffett and Bernard Arnault both fell out of Forbes' top 10 in August as Berkshire and LVMH shares slid. Michael Dell and Steve Ballmer moved in.
Greg Abel sold Berkshire's Visa and Mastercard stakes in the second quarter and kept American Express.
Larry Page recently bought a home in Florida, reportedly in response to California's push to tax billionaires.
memo: Meta and Nvidia are both spending to own more of the AI stack. Expect the tools your business uses to get bundled into fewer, bigger platforms.
AI agents that shop for people are coming to glasses and pocket devices. If you sell anything, think about how an AI would find and book you.
The most patient buyer in the market is sitting on about $365B in cash. Keep your own reserves honest.
